title: Amortized Complexity and Invariant Preservation in a Ruby Fibonacci Heap Implementation
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a Ruby implementation of the Fibonacci Heap, a balanced search and indexing structure that supports insert, extract-min, and decrease-key in amortized $O(1)$, $O(\log n)$, and $O(1)$ time respectively. The design preserves strict height-balance and key-ordered invariants through root consolidation and cascading cuts. We formally prove that the heap maintains a logarithmic bound on the maximum root degree and that all operations respect the heap order. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 9V74 80-core processor (1 physical core, 2 logical threads) yields a mean latency of 113 754.93 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 8 791 ops/s over 30 iterations. The source code is publicly available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/ruby-algorithms-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261115_070238_advanced_algorithms}.
